exposure: Pregnancy with a stoma (in women with IBD)
outcome: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (prematurity, low birth weight, dysmaturity, pregnancy loss)
cohort: Fifty pregnant patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and a stoma, who delivered between 2016 and 2023 in 5 Dutch university hospitals.
finding: Pregnancy in women with a stoma is feasible, but stoma-related complications, most commonly obstruction, frequently occur (71.0%) and often require management, though they are mostly manageable.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were performed in 50.0% of the pregnancies.
followup_time: Up to 1 year postpartum (for stoma-related surgery) and 6 months postpartum (for patient-reported complications)
birth_weight: Low birth weight was observed in 14.5% of pregnancies.
gest_age: Prematurity was observed in 14.5% of pregnancies; 71.0% were full-term pregnancies.
